general.fact: Anonymity is mostly gone. The NYT co-chief critics and the new WaPo critic dine openly. Reservation apps and social media make hiding nearly impossible.
Open critics still book under other names and pay their own way. Expect a reservation name that does not match the face.
Critics make several visits before a review. Pete Wells usually went three times, each time with three friends.
After the visits, the NYT calls the restaurant for fact-checking and photos. That call means a review is coming soon.
Michelin inspectors stay anonymous, book under assumed names, take no notes at the table, and pay in full. Each eats 250+ meals a year.
A Michelin inspector may reveal themselves only after paying, for example to ask questions or see the kitchen.
Michelin stars need agreement among the inspectors. Disagreement means more visits.
Treat every guest the same. The safest plan is consistent service, not spotting critics.
